steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
At a high level, a Transformer processes a sequence by letting every position “look at” every other position through self-attention, then refining those interactions with small feed-forward networks—and it repeats those two steps in a stack of layers. Here’s the flow:

1. Input tokens → embeddings + positional encodings (so order matters).
2. In each layer, compute for each position:
   • Queries, Keys, Values via learned linear projections.
   • Attention scores = softmax(Query·Keyᵀ/√d) → weighted sum of Values.
   • Multi-head: run several attention heads in parallel for different subspaces.
3. Add & normalize, then pass through a point-wise feed-forward network.
4. Add & normalize again.
5. Repeat N layers.

For generation (in a decoder), you add masked self-attention (to prevent “peeking” ahead) and cross-attention over encoder outputs. This design captures long-range dependencies efficiently and in parallel.
